questions.questionText: A company has 1000 preference shares of Rs 100 (dividend 8%) and 7000 equity shares of Rs 10. Rs 50000 is available for dividends. After paying preference shareholders first, the rest goes to equity holders. What dividend rate do equity shareholders get?

questions.explanation: Dividend per share = 0.9. Shares needed = 4500/0.9 = 5000. Investment = 5000 x 15 = Rs 75000.
questions.shortcut: Find dividend per share, shares needed, then multiply by the market price.

questions.questionText: A company pays a dividend of 15% on shares of face value Rs 100. A man owns shares worth Rs 95000 (at face value). What is his yearly dividend?
questions.explanation: Dividend = 15% of Rs 95000 = Rs 14250.
questions.shortcut: Take 15% of the total face value.

questions.questionText: A company pays a dividend of 12% on shares of face value Rs 100. A man owns shares worth Rs 200000 (at face value). What is his yearly dividend?
questions.explanation: Dividend = 12% of Rs 200000 = Rs 24000.
questions.shortcut: Take 12% of the total face value.

questions.questionText: Rs 40000 is invested in a 10% stock (face value Rs 100) at 125. What is the annual income?
questions.explanation: Income = investment x rate / market value = 40000 x 10 / 125 = Rs 3200.
questions.shortcut: Annual income = investment x rate / market value.

questions.questionText: A man sells Rs 32000 of 10% stock at 100 and reinvests the proceeds in 15% stock at 80. By how much does his annual income increase? Choose the correct statement.
questions.explanation: Old income = 320 x 10 = 3200. Proceeds = Rs 32000; new income = 32000 x 15/80 = 6000. Change = 2800: increase of Rs 2800.
questions.shortcut: Compute old and new income and subtract.

questions.questionText: A man owns 1750 shares of Rs 100 each, currently quoted at Rs 110 each. The company declares a 15% dividend. What total dividend does he receive?
questions.explanation: Dividend is paid on face value, not market value: 1750 x 100 x 15/100 = Rs 26250.
questions.shortcut: Market value never enters the dividend: only face value and the rate.

questions.questionText: A man owns 100 shares of Rs 100 each, currently quoted at Rs 105 each. The company declares a 20% dividend. What total dividend does he receive?

questions.questionText: A man sells Rs 8000 of 8% stock at 100 and reinvests the proceeds in 12% stock at 125. By how much does his annual income increase? Choose the correct statement.
questions.explanation: Old income = 80 x 8 = 640. Proceeds = Rs 8000; new income = 8000 x 12/125 = 768. Change = 128: increase of Rs 128.
questions.shortcut: Compute old and new income and subtract.
